title:
Clinical Scanning
Workflow
subtitle: Redesigning the clinical scanning workflow for speed, clarity, and decision-making in real treatment conditions.

slides.title:
Clinical Scanning
Workflow
slides.description:
The patient is in the chair. The scanner is ready. The system isn't.
iTero is a digital intraoral scanner used chairside during live patient appointments. I redesigned Align Technology's RX, Scan, and View workflow into one continuous system.
slides.presenterNotes: אז הקייס הזה הוא על iTero — סורק תוך־פה דיגיטלי של אליין טכנולוגיס. הצוות שלי עיצב מחדש את כל זרימת העבודה — מההגדרה של המקרה ועד הוולידציה לפני המעבדה. כל זה תוך כדי שהמטופל יושב בכיסא. עבדתי על זה שלושה חודשים עם מנהל מוצר וארבעה מפתחים.

slides.label: The System
slides.title: A system used during live patient treatment
slides.content: iTero is used chair-side. Three phases — RX, Scan, View — feed into each other. A problem in one disrupts the whole appointment.
issues: RX → define patient, procedure, case details
Scan → capture a real-time 3D model
View → validate before lab submission
slides.highlight: Every decision happens under time pressure — with the patient in the chair.
slides.presenterNotes: לפני שאני נכנס לבעיה, חשוב להבין איך המערכת עובדת. יש שלושה שלבים — RX, סריקה, וצפייה — שכל אחד מזין את השני. הכל קורה צ'יירסייד, עם המטופל בחדר. כל החלטה היא תחת לחץ זמן, כי מישהו מחכה לך בכיסא.

slides.label: The Problem
slides.title: The Rx was a form. The clinic isn't.
slides.content: Sequential, popup-heavy, and rigid — it forced clinical decisions before clinicians had the information to make them.
issues: Every tooth, material, and spec triggered a modal
No multi-select — procedures set tooth by tooth
Changing a procedure meant starting over
Setup had to finish before scanning could begin
slides.highlight: Every popup happened with a patient watching.
slides.presenterNotes: הבעיה הייתה שה־RX נבנה כמו טופס — שלב אחרי שלב, עם המון פופאפים, ובלי גמישות. כל שן וכל חומר פתחו חלון נפרד. ואם רצית לשנות פרוצדורה באמצע — היית צריך להתחיל מההתחלה. בעצם הטופס הזה הכריח את הרופא לקבל החלטות לפני שהיה לו את המידע.

slides.label: Who It Affected
slides.title: The problem reached further than the chair
slides.description: Setup failures didn't stop at the clinician. Every incomplete field and blocking modal sent ripple effects downstream.

issues.title: Dentists
issues.description: Every extra click was time not spent on the patient — setup friction happened chair-side, with the patient watching.

issues.title: Clinical staff
issues.description: Incomplete cases and mandatory-field errors generated resubmissions — administrative work created by avoidable UI gaps.

issues.title: Labs
issues.description: Received Rx data that was incomplete or unstructured for complex procedures like All-on-X and multi-phase treatments.

slides.presenterNotes: הבעיה לא נעצרה אצל הרופא. כשהמילוי היה לא מלא, הצוות הקליני היה צריך להגיש מקרים מחדש. והמעבדות קיבלו מידע חסר על מקרים מורכבים כמו All-on-X. אז אם הרופא עיכב — כל השרשרת אחריו עיכבה.

slides.label: Why Now
slides.title: Three signals converged at once
slides.content: 3Shape, Medit, and Shining3D had already modernised their Rx flows. The iTero architecture had been patched too many times to patch again — the only path forward was a rebuild.
issues: Competitors had modernised — iTero's Rx flow was visibly behind
At this scale, every extra popup per case was expensive
The codebase couldn't absorb another patch — only a rebuild would hold
slides.highlight: At 37 million cases a year, one unnecessary popup per case adds up fast.
slides.presenterNotes: שלושה דברים התכנסו באותו זמן. המתחרים — 3Shape, Medit, Shining3D — כבר עברו דורות של עדכון. הקוד של iTero כבר לא הצליח לסבול עוד טלאי. ובקנה המידה של אליין — 37 מיליון מקרים בשנה — אפילו פופאפ מיותר אחד למקרה זה כסף וזמן עצום. זה היה הרגע לבנות מחדש, לא לתקן.

slides.label: Research & Discovery
slides.title: What I heard in the room
slides.content: I interviewed doctors across procedure types — restorative specialists, general dentists, orthodontists. I asked each one to walk me through a real case: where they slowed down, what they wished worked differently. Five themes came back in every session.

quotes.text: It feels like a long boring form — and I'm doing it with a patient in the chair.
quotes.author: Restorative Specialist

quotes.text: I change the procedure multiple times before I even begin scanning.
quotes.author: General Dentist

quotes.text: There's always another popup. I just want to get to the scan.
quotes.author: Orthodontist

quotes.text: Every time I select a tooth, something opens. I can't see what I've already done.
quotes.author: Restorative Specialist

quotes.text: The moment I go looking for a tool, I lose my rhythm completely.
quotes.author: General Dentist

slides.presenterNotes: ראיינתי רופאים משלושה תחומים — שיקום, רפואת שיניים כללית, ואורתודנטיה. ביקשתי מכל אחד לקחת אותי דרך מקרה אמיתי. מה שמעניין זה שהם לא התלוננו — הם פשוט קיבלו את החיכוך הזה כחלק מהעבודה. חמישה מוטיבים חזרו אצל כולם.

slides.label: Pain Points
slides.title: Four pain points, four design moves
description: Five themes from the interviews, clustered into four problems the redesign had to solve. Each one became a design direction.

issues.title: Setup blocks the scan
issues.description: Clinicians had to finish a long, popup-heavy form before scanning could begin — with the patient watching. Fix: setup that runs alongside the scan, not before it.

issues.title: Procedure locked in too early
issues.description: Clinicians often changed the procedure several times before scanning — but every change meant starting over. Fix: procedure that can be picked or swapped in one tap, before scanning starts.

issues.title: Tooth-by-tooth, with no visibility
issues.description: Every tooth opened its own modal. Clinicians couldn't see what they'd already configured. Fix: multi-select directly on the dental chart, with procedures visible at a glance.

issues.title: Tools scattered across the screen
issues.description: Clinicians lost their rhythm searching for tools mid-scan — no dedicated home, no shared visual language. Fix: one toolbar with one icon system.

slides.presenterNotes: אחרי הראיונות לקחתי את חמישה המוטיבים שחזרו וגיבשתי אותם לארבע נקודות כאב. כל אחת מתחברת ישירות לפתרון שאני אראה בהמשך. ההגדרה חוסמת את הסריקה, הפרוצדורה ננעלת מוקדם מדי, בחירת השיניים אחת־אחת בלי שקיפות, והכלים מפוזרים בלי בית. כל אחת קיבלה תשובה עיצובית.

slides.label: User Flow Mapping
slides.title: What clinicians actually do — not what the product assumed
slides.content: The research surfaced what hurt. Mapping the flow showed where each complaint lived — and the friction clustered at the handoffs between phases.
issues: RX → Scan: setup blocked the clinician before any scan began
Scan → View: tool access broke the clinician's rhythm mid-capture
View → submit: no completion signal — View felt unfinished
slides.issuesTitle: Three breakpoints — one per phase handoff
slides.highlight: The interviews told me what hurt. The flow told me where to fix it.

image.caption: Appointment flow map — three handoffs, three breakpoints

slides.presenterNotes: אחרי הראיונות, מיפיתי את הזרימה האמיתית שרופאים עוברים — לא איך המוצר חשב שהם עוברים. שלוש נקודות שבר צצו, וכולן באותו מקום — בין השלבים. בעצם החיכוך לא היה אקראי, הוא היה במעברים. זה היה הרגע שהבנתי שזו לא בעיה של טופס, זו בעיה של ארכיטקטורה.

slides.label: Design Goals
slides.title: Goals by phase

goals.title: Configuration in one step
goals.description: Multi-select teeth, group materials, one interaction.

goals.title: Scanning stays uninterrupted
goals.description: Tools accessible without leaving the capture.

goals.title: One visual language
goals.description: No icon memorisation, no mixed styles.

kpis: Time to find the right tool
slides.presenterNotes: חילקתי את המטרות לפי שלב — שתיים ל־RX, שתיים ל־Scan & View. כל מטרה צמודה ל־KPI שאני יכול למדוד, כולל מדידה ישירה של כמה popups חוסמים נשארו במסלול הקליני. הכל מתחבר ישירות לפרקים שאני אראה בהמשך.

slides.label: Constraints
slides.title: What I kept in mind while designing

issues.title: Three surfaces
issues.description: Scanner (touch-only, gloved hands), MIDC desktop, and web — hover works with a mouse, but the scanner can't rely on it.

issues.title: Backward compatibility
issues.description: Old Rx stayed live for in-progress cases.

issues.title: Feature-flagged
issues.description: On or off per company — learnable on first contact, every time.

issues.title: Read and demo states
issues.description: Three states designed in from day one — not retrofitted.

description:
Not every constraint forced a specific decision
but each one stayed in the back of my mind while designing, 
shaping what felt safe to ship across all three surfaces.
slides.presenterNotes: היו ארבעה דברים שלא יכולתי לשנות. צריך לעצב לשלושה משטחים שונים — הסורק עצמו שעובד רק במגע ועם כפפות, מחשב נייח, ו־web. ה־RX הישן היה צריך להמשיך לרוץ למקרים שכבר באמצע. הפיצ'ר היה ב־flag, יכול להיות פתוח או סגור לפי חברה. ומצב קריאה ודמו היו צריכים להיות מעוצבים מהיום הראשון, לא משהו שמוסיפים בסוף.

slides.label: Interactive Prototype
slides.title: A coded prototype to test decisions before development
slides.content: Figma shows what a screen looks like — it can't show how the workflow feels. I built the prototype in code so flow and timing problems surfaced before any screen was locked.
bullets2: Flow problems caught before any screen was locked
Test and adjust options live — no waiting on a new Figma file
Faster iteration — change something, see it work, decide
slides.highlight: Some design decisions can only be made in motion.
slides.presenterNotes: פיגמה מראה איך מסך נראה — היא לא מראה איך זרימה מרגישה. אז בניתי אב־טיפוס בקוד עוד לפני שנעלתי משהו ב־Figma. ככה תפסתי בעיות תזמון לפני שהן יקרות לתקן, ויכולתי לעשות שינוי בבוקר ולבחון אותו אחרי הצהריים. יש החלטות עיצוב שאי אפשר לקבל מתוך מסך סטטי.

slides.title: RX
slides.subtitle: Defining the patient, procedure, and case before scanning — and the setup gate I had to clear first.
slides.presenterNotes: נכנסים לפרק הראשון — RX. זה השלב שבו רופא מגדיר את המטופל ואת הפרוצדורה לפני הסריקה. זה היה השער שהייתי צריך לפתוח לפני כל השאר.

slides.label: RX Setup — Before
slides.title: Setup blocked the scan before it could start
slides.content: The old product was a dense, multi-step form — patient and procedure gated behind blocking modals before scanning could begin. Every change opened another popup.
issues: Patient selection required a multi-step modal
Changing a procedure triggered a blocking popup every time
Dropdown disconnected from the dental chart — no visual link to teeth
Procedure had to be defined upfront, before any scan data existed
slides.highlight: Every second here was a second the patient sat waiting.
slides.caption: Old RX setup — the blocking multi-step form.
slides.presenterNotes: ככה זה נראה לפני. טופס דחוס, מודאל לבחירת מטופל, פופאפ חוסם בכל שינוי פרוצדורה, ודרופ־דאון שלא היה מחובר לתרשים השיניים. כל שנייה פה זאת שנייה שהמטופל ישב וחיכה.

slides.label: RX Setup — Low-Fidelity Wireframes
slides.title: Three structures, sketched before any polish
slides.dir1Desc: Wizard. Step-by-step, one decision per screen. Easy to test the boundary — does step-gating help or hurt under chairside pressure?
slides.dir2Desc: Accordion. Everything on one screen, but collapsed by default. Open what you need, leave the rest closed.
slides.dir3Desc: Single view. Everything visible at once — no steps, no walls. The riskiest structurally, the simplest to use.
slides.description: Before any polish, I sketched the three structural options as wireframes — the cheapest way to ask which form model actually fit chairside use. All three got built. All three got tested with clinicians.
slides.presenterNotes: לפני שהשקעתי בעיצוב מלא, סקיצתי את שלוש האפשרויות כ־wireframes. רציתי לבדוק איזה מבנה עובד בלחץ של חדר טיפולים — בלי להתחייב לכיוון אחד. כל שלושת המבנים נבחנו עם רופאים אמיתיים, ורק אז ידעתי לאן ללכת בפיתוח מלא.

slides.label: RX Setup — Exploration
slides.title: Three approaches — tested with clinicians on real cases
slides.dir1Desc: Step-by-step wizard. Organised, but clinicians felt railroaded — too rigid for chairside use.
slides.dir2Desc: Collapse/expand layout — tap to open, read, close, repeat. In practice, clinicians reopened the same section constantly.
slides.dir3Desc: Everything visible at once — no steps, no walls. Same fields, same order as before — just nothing in the way.
slides.presenterNotes: בחנתי שלושה כיוונים עם רופאים אמיתיים. הראשון, ויזרד בצעדים — מאורגן, אבל הרגיש שהוא מנהל אותם. השני, אקורדיון שנפתח ונסגר — בפועל פתחו וסגרו את אותו חלק שוב ושוב. הכיוון שעבר היה הכל גלוי במסך אחד — אותם שדות, אותו סדר, פשוט בלי קירות בין השלבים. רופאים הבינו אותו מיד כי התהליך נשאר מוכר.

slides.label: RX Setup — After
slides.title: Setup runs alongside the scan — not before it
slides.content: Same fields, same order — just no walls between them. The setup is shorter, the menus aren't buried, and the actions that mattered most are visible at a glance.
issues: Single view — no modals, no popups, less scrolling
Change procedure easily — pick or swap in one tap
New patient created from a dedicated, always-visible entry
slides.caption: New RX setup — single-view, no blocking form, much less scrolling.
slides.presenterNotes: וזאת התוצאה. אותם שדות, אותו סדר — פשוט בלי הקירות. ההגדרה התקצרה, פחות גלילה, יצירת מטופל חדש עברה למקום ייעודי, ועכשיו אפשר לבחור הרבה שיניים בבחירה אחת. הרופאים לא צריכים ללמוד משהו חדש — הם פשוט הפסיקו להילחם בטופס.

slides.label: RX Tooth Selection
slides.title: Multi-select replaced one at a time
slides.beforeDescription: Every tooth needed its own modal — click, confirm, close, repeat.
slides.afterDescription: Teeth selected directly on the chart — one or many at once — with procedures assigned inline.
slides.presenterNotes: כאן הלפני־ואחרי של בחירת שיניים. לפני — מודאל לכל שן, אחת אחת. אחרי — בחירה ישירה על התרשים, עם הפרוצדורות בצבעים. בעצם תוכנית הטיפול גלויה לגמרי בלי לפתוח שום דבר.

slides.title: Scan & View
slides.subtitle: Capture and validation treated as one continuous phase — the clinician never leaves the screen between them.
slides.presenterNotes: פרק שני. ויש פה החלטה עיצובית — במקור Scan ו־View היו שני שלבים נפרדים. אבל בפועל הרופא לא חווה אותם ככה — הוא לא יוצא מהמסך ביניהם. אז איחדתי אותם לפרק אחד.

slides.label: Scan Toolbar — Before
slides.title: Tools scattered, with no home
slides.content: Icons built up from different eras, different styles, no shared visual language — and no consistent place to find them mid-scan.
issues: No shared visual language across icons
No dedicated place for tools
Every new feature added more scatter
slides.highlight: A clinician shouldn't have to find a tool — the tool should find them.
slides.caption: Old toolbar — scattered, mixed-style icons.
slides.presenterNotes: תראו איך נראתה מערכת הכלים לפני. אייקונים נצברו לאורך השנים, סגנונות שונים, ובלי מקום ייעודי לכלים. רופא לא צריך לחפש כלי באמצע סריקה — הכלי צריך להיות שם איפה שהוא יודע למצוא אותו.

slides.question: How can every tool live in one place — without ever getting in the doctor's way?
slides.support: A single home tools could scale into, predictable enough that clinicians never had to look for it — and never had to fight it mid-scan.
slides.presenterNotes: השאלה שהובילה את הפרק הזה. הבעיה לא הייתה איפה אייקונים נראים יפה. היא הייתה איפה רופא יכול להגיע לכלי בלי לעזוב את הסריקה. יד אחת על ה־wand, עיניים נעולות על המודל. השאלה — איך כל כלי חי במקום אחד, בלי להפריע, עם מקום שהרופא יודע שהוא יהיה שם.

slides.label: Looking Outward
slides.title: How other platforms solved the same problem
slides.content: Instead of inventing something new, I looked at how other software handles tools that need to live in one place. Every platform with a lot of tools used the same pattern — a toolbar.
issues: One dedicated location for tools
A pattern that scales as new tools get added
Out of the way of the work, but always findable
slides.highlight: The format wasn't a guess — it's how platforms with lots of tools have always solved this.
slides.presenterNotes: במקום להמציא משהו חדש, הסתכלתי איך תוכנות אחרות פותרות את אותה בעיה. בכל פלטפורמה עם הרבה כלים — הפתרון היה אותו דבר, toolbar. אז זה לא ניחוש, זה דפוס מוכח. המשימה שלי הייתה ליישם אותו טוב להקשר קליני, לא להמציא מחדש.

slides.label: Toolbar — Exploration
slides.title: Once the toolbar was the answer, the question became where to put it
slides.dir1Desc: Bottom center. Sat across the occlusal area — and some clinicians had to stretch to reach it depending on how they were positioned.
slides.dir2Desc: Vertical right rail. Always visible, but it overlapped and competed with other tools — interfering with controls clinicians already used.
slides.dir3Desc: Top-right corner. The only position clinicians could reach without pulling their eyes off the model — out of the scan area, out of the way.
slides.presenterNotes: בחנתי שלושה מיקומים. למטה במרכז — ישב על האזור שדווקא היה צריך להיראות, וגם רחוק להגיע. ימין־אנכי — תמיד גלוי, אבל התנגש עם כלים שכבר היו במסך. ימין־עליון, קולאפסיבל — היה המיקום היחיד שרופאים יכלו להגיע אליו בלי להוריד עיניים מהמודל. כיוון שעבר.

slides.label: Scan Toolbar — After
slides.title: One toolbar, one visual language
slides.content: A top-right toolbar — out of the scan area, always findable. Icons rebuilt as one system: consistent line weight, consistent style, labeled.
issues: Toolbar fixed to one corner — always findable
New tools slot in without requiring new conventions
bullets2: Toolbar and procedure icons rebuilt as one visual system
Consistent line weight and style across every tool
slides.highlight: Placement and language solved together — not in sequence.
slides.caption: New top-right toolbar + unified icon set.
slides.presenterNotes: אז ככה זה נראה בסוף. Toolbar ימין־עליון, מחוץ לאזור הסריקה, תמיד נמצא. ובנוסף, האייקונים נבנו מחדש כמערכת אחת — אותו עובי, אותו סגנון, עם תיוג. הנקודה החשובה — המיקום והשפה נפתרו ביחד. אם פותרים רק מיקום ואייקונים לא קריאים — עדיין יש בעיה.

slides.label: Multi-scan & Compare
slides.title: Managing multiple scans and comparing them
slides.content: Complex cases need pre-treatment, treatment, and additional reference scans. Tabs scaled with the case and clinicians already knew the pattern. Overlay with adjustable opacity shows reduction prep, fit, and alignment side by side.
bullets2: Tabs scale with the case — a pattern clinicians already know
Overlay scans with adjustable opacity — see reduction prep, fit, and alignment
What clinicians used to hold in memory, now visible on screen
slides.presenterNotes: מקרים מורכבים דורשים יותר מסריקה אחת — לפני, אחרי, וסריקות עזר. השתמשתי ב־tabs כי הם גדלים עם המקרה, וגם כי רופאים כבר מכירים את הדפוס. עכשיו אפשר להניח שני סריקות זו על זו עם opacity ולראות בדיוק מה השתנה — בלי להחזיק את ההשוואה בראש.

slides.label: View Tools
slides.title: From icon bars to clinical decision panels
slides.beforeDescription: Unlabelled icon clusters with no hierarchy — every meaning memorised, nothing self-explanatory.
slides.afterDescription: Named panels with one clear primary action — the same structure across every tool, nothing to memorise.
slides.presenterNotes: כלי הצפייה לפני־ואחרי. לפני — אשכולות אייקונים בלי תיוג, רופאים היו צריכים לזכור מה כל אייקון עושה. אחרי — פאנלים עם שם וקריאה ראשית אחת לכל כלי, מבנה זהה בכל אחד. אין יותר עצירה ומחשבה מה זה.

slides.label: Design System
slides.title: Every component built in three states from the start
slides.content: Every pattern from the redesign became a reusable component — built in three states (editable, read-only, demo) and pushed to Storybook so engineering had a single source of truth.
slides.highlight: The three-state architecture became the shared language the rest of the product was built on.

image.caption: Design system components formalised from the redesign

slides.presenterNotes: תוצר נוסף של הפרויקט. כל דפוס שיצא מהעיצוב הפך לקומפוננטה רב־פעמית — בנויה מההתחלה בשלושה מצבים: עריכה, קריאה, ודמו. אם הייתי מוסיף את מצב הקריאה אחר כך, היה לי אי־עקביות בכל המוצר — וזה לא מקובל בהקשר רפואי. הכל נדחף ל־Storybook כדי שלהנדסה תהיה אמת אחת.

slides.label: Outcomes
slides.title: Four goals, Four outcomes — what changed in measurable terms

outcomes.title: Multi-tooth selection in one step
outcomes.description: Select a range, apply procedure and material in one interaction.

outcomes.title: Scrolling and buried menus
outcomes.description: Shorter setup view — procedure, patient, and teeth all swappable in seconds.

outcomes.title: Scanning stays in rhythm
outcomes.description: Toolbar fixed in one corner — tools reachable without leaving the scan.

outcomes.title: One visual language across every tool
outcomes.description: Unified icon set replaced scattered styles — each tool reads at a glance.

slides.presenterNotes: התוצאות מתחברות ישירות למטרות שהצבתי בהתחלה. חמש מטרות, חמש תוצאות. השער הוסר מהסריקה, אפשר לבחור הרבה שיניים בצעד אחד, אפס מודאלים חוסמים במסלול הקריטי, סריקה ממשיכה ברצף, ושפה חזותית אחת. חשוב לציין — אלה תוצאות מאומתות בבדיקות פרוטוטיפ. מטריקות מהשטח עוד מגיעות אחרי השקה מלאה.

slides.label: Reflection
slides.title: What I took away
whatWorked: Hands-on development — building parts of the UI myself meant faster rollout and quicker UX QA.
Borrowing proven patterns — toolbar and tabs from products clinicians already use. Familiar over novel.
Cross-functional negotiation — technical discussions with engineering shaped scope without degrading the experience.
whatFailed: Jumped into design before fully learning the clinical world — had to go back to clinicians for terms and daily flow I missed.
Showed the new icons individually before showing the full toolbar — clinicians rejected them in isolation, only accepted the system once they saw it together.
Tooth chart took multiple rounds — making it scalable for complex cases while keeping the familiar context took longer than scoped.
whatYoudDoDifferently: Spend more time with clinicians before opening Figma — understand the world first, design second.
Validate systems in context, not in isolation — show the whole pattern, not the parts.
Add an AI assistant to the RX — drafting notes and procedure suggestions as the clinician works.
slides.whatYouCouldntMeasure: Outcomes were validated in prototype testing, not the field. Post-launch metrics still pending.
slides.whatYouLearned: Getting the diagnosis right before Figma shaped everything — and choosing familiar patterns made the rest of the work cheaper to ship.
slides.presenterNotes: מה עבד — פיתוח חלקים מה־UI לבד כדי לזרז QA, שאילה של דפוסים מוכחים במקום להמציא, ומשא ומתן עם הנדסה על scope בלי לפגוע בחוויה. מה לא עבד — קפצתי לעיצוב לפני שלמדתי מספיק את העולם הקליני, והצגתי אייקונים בנפרד לפני שהראיתי את המערכת השלמה. בפעם הבאה — יותר זמן עם רופאים לפני שאני פותח Figma, ולאמת מערכות בהקשר, לא בבידוד. ויש כיוון אחד שאני אוסיף — עוזר AI ב־RX שיכתוב הערות והצעות פרוצדורה בזמן שהרופא עובד.

slides.title: Thank You
slides.subtitle: The real solution wasn't Rx—it was rethinking the architecture.
slides.presenterNotes: אז זאת השורה הכי חשובה של כל הפרויקט. ה־RX נראה כמו בעיה של טופס. אבל זאת הייתה בעיה של ארכיטקטורה. הסיבה היחידה שהצלחתי לפתור את זה הייתה שזיהיתי את האבחנה הנכונה לפני שהתחלתי לעצב.

article.title: Clinical Scanning Workflow
article.lede: The patient is in the chair. The scanner is ready. The system isn't. I redesigned Align Technology's RX, Scan and View workflow on iTero into one continuous system.

items.label: Problem
items.text: iTero's Rx was a sequential, popup-heavy form that had to be completed before scanning could start — every tooth opened its own modal, and changing a procedure meant starting over. All of it happened chairside, with the patient watching.

items.label: Solution
items.text: Setup rebuilt as a single view that runs alongside the scan instead of gating it, with multi-select directly on the dental chart, and every tool consolidated into one fixed toolbar under a single icon system.

items.label: Impact
items.text: Blocking popups removed from the setup path, procedure and teeth swappable in seconds, and every pattern formalised into a three-state component library in Storybook.

blocks.text: Context: a system used during live patient treatment

iTero is a digital intraoral scanner used chairside. Three phases feed into each other — **RX** defines the patient, procedure and case details; **Scan** captures a real-time 3D model; **View** validates it before lab submission. A problem in one doesn't stay there. It disrupts the whole appointment.
Every decision happens under time pressure — with the patient in the chair.
The problem: a long setup form stood between the clinician and the scan

The setup was sequential, popup-heavy and rigid — it forced clinical decisions before clinicians had the information to make them. And the cost didn't stop at the chair: incomplete cases generated resubmissions for clinical staff, and labs received Rx data that was unstructured for complex procedures like All-on-X.

media.caption: The old Rx — modal-gated, tooth by tooth

annotations.text: A long form had to be done before scanning — with the patient watching
Clinicians changed the procedure several times — each change meant starting over
Every tooth opened a modal — no multi-select, no view of what was set

quotes.text: It feels like a long boring form — and I'm doing it with a patient in the chair.
quotes.author: Restorative Specialist

quotes.text: Every time I select a tooth, something opens. I can't see what I've already done.
quotes.author: Restorative Specialist

quotes.text: The moment I go looking for a tool, I lose my rhythm completely.
quotes.author: General Dentist

blocks.text: Why now: years of patches had outgrown the architecture

3Shape, Medit and Shining3D had already modernised their Rx flows, so iTero's was visibly behind. More importantly, the codebase couldn't absorb another patch — the only path forward was a rebuild. And at this volume, friction isn't cosmetic.
At 37 million cases a year, one unnecessary popup per case adds up fast.
Flow mapping: the friction clustered between steps

I interviewed clinicians across procedure types — restorative specialists, general dentists, orthodontists — and asked each to walk me through a real case. Mapping what they described against the product showed the complaints weren't spread evenly. They gathered at the three points where one phase hands off to the next.

media.caption: Appointment flow map — three handoffs, three breakpoints

annotations.text: Rx → Scan: setup blocked the clinician before any scan could begin
Scan → View: tool access broke the clinician's rhythm mid-capture

blocks.text: Design goals: what the redesign had to fix

items: **Configuration in one step** — multi-select teeth, group materials, one interaction.
**Less scrolling, easier to change** — shorter view, no buried menus.
**Scanning stays uninterrupted** — tools reachable without leaving the capture.
**One visual language** — no icon memorisation, no mixed styles.

blocks.title: How we'd know it worked
items: Average teeth per interaction
Scroll depth in RX setup
Blocking popups per case
Time to find the right tool

blocks.text: Method: a coded prototype to test the timing

Figma shows what a screen looks like. It can't show how a workflow feels under time pressure, which was the entire problem here. So I built the prototype in code — flow and timing issues surfaced before any screen was locked, and options could be adjusted live during a session instead of waiting on a new file.
Decision 1: three ways to structure the setup form
The first breakpoint was the Rx itself. Its structure decides everything downstream, so I sketched three models as wireframes, built all three, and tested each with clinicians on real cases.
Step-by-step wizard
One decision per screen, in a fixed order.

annotations.text: One thing to answer at a time
Required fields can't be skipped — fewer incomplete cases reach the lab
Organised, but clinicians felt railroaded by the fixed order

blocks.text: Collapsed accordion
Everything on one screen, but closed by default — open what you need, leave the rest shut.

annotations.text: Short screen, full access — no steps to traverse
New sections slot in without lengthening the page
Tap to open, read, close, repeat

blocks.text: Single view
Everything visible at once. Same fields, same order as before — nothing in the way.

annotations.text: Setup no longer gates the scan — it continues alongside capture
Nothing is hidden — any part of the case can be changed at any moment

blocks.text: We chose the single view, based on explicit tradeoffs. Visibility was critical for chairside use — clinicians revise constantly and can't afford to hunt for what they set. But the density and completeness concerns were real, and we resolved them before committing.
Rx after: setup runs alongside the scan, not before it

Same fields, same order — just no walls between them. Procedure and patient are swappable in a tap, and teeth are selected directly on the chart, one or many at a time, with procedures assigned inline.

media.caption: New RX setup — single view, no blocking form, far less scrolling

blocks.text: Tooth selection: multi-select instead of one tooth at a time

Removing the walls around the form didn't fix what happened inside it. The dental chart was still the densest interaction in the Rx — and the one clinicians repeated most, since a single case can involve a full arch. Nothing else in the setup was touched as often, so it needed its own answer.
Before
The dropdown that assigned the spec sat apart from the chart, so the clinician never saw the case as a whole.

media.caption: Before — one modal per tooth, with no view of what was already set

annotations.text: Eight teeth meant eight dialogs — click, confirm, close, repeat
No visual link between a tooth and what was assigned to it

blocks.text: After

Teeth are selected directly on the chart — tap one, or shift-click a range — and the procedure and material are assigned inline to the whole selection. The chart itself became the record: what's configured is visible on the tooth, so the clinician reads the case instead of remembering it.

blocks.title: How it works
items: **Tap or range-select** — one tooth or a full arch, in a single interaction.
**Specs assigned inline** — crown, bridge, veneer, inlay applied to the whole selection at once.
**State visible on the chart** — every configured tooth reads at a glance, with no modal to reopen.
**Revisable at any point** — change a selection or a spec without unwinding the rest of the case.

media.caption: After — multi-select on the chart, procedures assigned inline

blocks.text: Scan toolbar before: tools scattered with no fixed home

Icons had built up across different product eras and different styles, with no shared visual language — and no consistent place to find them mid-scan. Every clinician who paused to look for a tool paused with a patient in the chair.

blocks.title: Where it broke
items: **Every new feature added more scatter** — with no system to slot into, each addition landed wherever there was room.

annotations.text: Icons drawn in different eras, at different weights
No fixed home — finding a tool mid‑scan meant scanning the whole screen

blocks.text: A clinician shouldn't have to find a tool — the tool should be where they already are.
Toolbar placement: three positions tested on the scan screen

Every platform with a large tool set had already settled the format — one dedicated location that scales as tools are added. Placement was the open question, and on a scan screen it's tightly constrained: the toolbar can't sit over the model, can't compete with controls already in use, and has to be reachable without the clinician looking away from the capture.
Bottom center

annotations.text: Closest to the hand, and the most conventional position
Sat across the occlusal area clinicians inspect most — and some had to stretch to reach it

blocks.text: Vertical right rail

annotations.text: Always visible, off the model — grows downward without limit
Same zone as controls already in use — it competed for space and attention

blocks.text: Top right

annotations.text: Out of the scan area, clear of existing controls, within reach without looking away
The trade-off: least conventional, and furthest from the hand

blocks.text: Placement alone wasn't enough. The icons had accumulated across product eras with no shared language, so I rebuilt the toolbar and procedure sets as one system — consistent line weight, consistent style, labelled — and solved position and language together rather than in sequence.

media.caption: New top-right toolbar and unified icon set

blocks.text: Multi-scan: managing and comparing several scans

Complex cases need more than one capture — pre-treatment, treatment, and additional reference scans. Tabs scale with the case and clinicians already knew the pattern, so nothing new had to be learned. Overlaying two scans with adjustable opacity puts reduction prep, fit and alignment side by side.

blocks.title: How it works
items: **Tabs scale with the case** — a pattern clinicians already know from everywhere else.
**Overlay with adjustable opacity** — see reduction prep, fit and alignment against each other.
**What clinicians used to hold in memory is now on screen** — the comparison stops being a mental exercise.

blocks.text: View tools: from icon bars to clinical decision panels

media.caption: Before - Unlabelled icon clusters with no hierarchy — every meaning memorised, nothing self-explanatory.
After — view tools as named panels

annotations.text: Each tool is a named panel with one clear primary action
Same structure across every tool — nothing to memorise

blocks.text: Design system: every component built in three states

Every pattern from the redesign became a reusable component — built in editable, read-only and demo states, and pushed to Storybook so engineering had a single source of truth rather than a set of screens to interpret.

media.caption: Design system components formalised from the redesign

blocks.text: Outcomes: what changed against the original goals

items: **Configuration in one step** — select a range of teeth, apply procedure and material in a single interaction.
**Setup stopped gating the scan** — blocking popups removed from the path, procedure and patient swappable in seconds.
**Scanning stays in rhythm** — the toolbar is fixed in one corner, reachable without leaving the capture.
**One visual language** — a unified icon set replaced the accumulated styles, so each tool reads at a glance.

blocks.text: Reflection: what I took away

worked: Building parts of the UI myself — faster rollout, and much quicker UX QA when I could fix things directly.
Borrowing proven patterns for the toolbar and tabs — familiar beat novel with clinicians under time pressure.
failed: I designed before I fully understood the clinical world, and had to go back to clinicians for terminology and daily flow I'd missed.
I showed the new icons individually before showing the full toolbar — clinicians rejected them in isolation and only accepted them as a system.
differently: Validate systems in context, never in isolation — show the whole pattern, not the parts.
Add an AI assistant to the RX, drafting notes and procedure suggestions as the clinician works.
